svg.title: MIDI Pedal Raspberry Pi Pico 2 wiring pinout
svg.desc: An infographic showing every physical Pico 2 header pin and the assigned connections for four footswitches, an ST7796S display, MIDI output, two relays, an expression pedal, USB, and power.
svg.text: Firmware GPIO assignments, physical header pins, and external connections
Normally-open contacts to ground • internal pull-ups
→ U2 current-limited driver → 3.5 mm TRS Type A
Type A: tip = DIN 5 sink • ring = DIN 4 source
sleeve = DIN 2 shield • never wire the jack directly to GPIO
Two independent normally-open, isolated dry contacts.
GPIOs drive transistor/coil stages—not the external contacts.
8 BL → always on • 9 SDA-0 / SDO → NC • logic remains 3.3 V
GP26 is physical pin 31 • voltage-divider pedals only.

text.tspan: VBUS pin 40 • native data; no GPIO

svg.text: USB provides CDC configuration + class-compliant USB-MIDI.

g.text: USB connector at top • top view
Sources: firmware/src/board/pico2_pins.hpp • hardware/bench/io-review.md • Raspberry Pi Pico 2 physical pinout
Logical GPIO assignments are authoritative. Carrier circuits, component values,
display VCC selection, and MIDI Type-A polarity still require ERC and bench verification.
This infographic is a wiring reference—not a fabrication drawing.
